messages:
alert-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api /v1/generate p95/p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2. queue_length=23400, gpu_pool=hosted-gpu-pool-us-west-2 @100% busy, autoscaler errors: "scale_limit_reached". dashboard: https://internal.metrics/redwood/hosted-api

emma (oncall): I'm oncall. paging eng-runtime and eng-sre. creating incident now. ping @raj @olivia :rotating_light:

raj: on it. can you paste the autoscaler logs and current pool state?

emma (oncall): logs (tail):
```
2026-03-14T11:02:12Z autoscaler ERROR scale_attempt failed: reason=quota_exceeded requested=8 available=0 pool=hosted-gpu-pool-us-west-2
2026-03-14T11:03:01Z serving WARN request_queue_length=23400 avg_wait_ms=2300 p95=6500 p99=14200
```
also running: `infractl pool describe hosted-gpu-pool-us-west-2` shows target=50 current=50 max=50

olivia: looks like autoscaler hit configured max or cloud quota. are nodes failing to boot? any boot errors from cloud?

jordan: checked cloud events — quota for A100 GPUs in us-west-2 for our org is 0 additional GPUs. provisioning requests are being rejected with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED: GPU quota` from provider. autoscaler is healthy but cannot provision new instances.

raj: that explains scale_limit_reached. we need immediate mitigations: 1) protect existing customers by throttling bursts 2) failover a subset of traffic to other region/pool 3) enable fallback to smaller models (cpu/4g-quantized) for best-effort requests.

mike (support): drafting external status: "We are experiencing elevated latency and intermittent timeouts for hosted API customers in us-west-2. Our team is actively mitigating. No data loss. If you have Dedicated capacity, traffic is unaffected." will share once we have ETA.

emma (oncall): implementing soft throttling on public routes now (rate-limit global burst from 2000rps -> 1200rps) to slow queue growth. applying via `deploy-bot` config: `rbctl config rate-limit set --service=hosted-api --burst=1200`

deploy-bot: rate-limit update accepted, propagating to edge (staged) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: I will flip routing for 20% of traffic to hosted-gpu-pool-us-east-1 and to fallback-model v-small-quant for non-SLA plans. executing runbook step: `routes override --svc=hosted-api --selector=region:us-east-1 --percent=20`

jordan: FYI we have capacity in us-east-1 but slower cold-start times. starting manual pool spin-up in us-west-2 isn't possible due to quota, trying request for quota increase with cloud but that's slow.

emma (oncall): @tim (product) any high-priority customers we should route differently?

tim (product): yes — enterprise customers with SLAs should be preserved. please exclude org IDs: org-87*, org-12* from fallback. notify their CSMs.

raj: routing applied. starting traffic shift 20% -> us-east-1 + fallback. monitoring...

(2m later)
raj: initial metrics: queue_length dropped from 23.4k -> 9.2k, p95 from 6.5s -> 2.1s, p99 improved from 14.2s -> 6.8s. still above target. throttling reducing incoming rate but backlog still drains slowly.

olivia: can we reduce batch window so each worker cycles faster? that might increase throughput for small seq lengths. but watch cost.

jordan: changed batching config for hosted-gpu-pool-us-west-2: `runtimectl set --pool=hosted-gpu-pool-us-west-2 --batch.max_ms=15` applied.

emma (oncall): notifying customers via status page now. mike please post the drafted message.

mike (support): posted status page update and emailed top 10 customers. CS Slack alerts sent.

raj: small wins: further p95 -> 1.6s, p99 -> 4.5s. queue at 3.1k. we still have cold-start variance affecting tail latency — some requests still hitting cold kernels in us-east-1.

emma (oncall): handing oncall to raj for active mitigation & postmortem. I'm stepping off in 30m. :hand:

raj: taking over. I'll keep this thread updated. @jordan can you keep pushing on quota request and escalate with cloud account team? we may need temporary quota or partner capacity.

jordan: opened high-priority support case with cloud, escalated to partner manager. ETA unknown (submitted 11:18 UTC). also preparing runbook to migrate some small models to CPU-only pools to relieve GPUs.

deploy-bot: canary config applied: fallback routing 20% -> us-east-1, rate-limits in place, batching reduced.

tim (product): coordinating comms for enterprise EAs. need a short summary for execs.

raj: summary for execs: GPU quota in us-west-2 exhausted causing autoscaler inability to scale. Traffic spike led to queue growth and P95/P99 latency degradation. Immediate mitigations: global soft throttles, route 20% traffic to us-east-1, enabled fallback smaller models for non-SLA, reduced batch latency. Partial mitigation achieved; user-impact reduced but not fully resolved.

mike (support): updated customer-facing status with mitigations and ETA placeholder. customers asked for credit — CS to triage after incident.

olivia: long tail still at p99 ~4.5s due to cold starts and remaining backlog. recommend follow-ups: 1) request quota increase + temp partner capacity 2) revisit autoscaler max settings and per-pool headroom 3) add better proactive quota monitoring for GPUs 4) improve cross-region routing automation.

raj: assigning postmortem owners: jor dan (eng-infra) and raj (eng-runtime). expected draft in 3 business days.

emma (oncall): thanks team. leaving handoff notes in pagerduty. :thumbsup:

mike (support): closing customer comms loop for now. will await postmortem for credits and root cause.

(incident status)
- impact: elevated latency and intermittent timeouts for hosted-api us-west-2 customers; some requests routed to fallback region/model.
- current state: degraded -> partial mitigation in place (throttles, routing, batching)
- next steps: quota escalation, postmortem, SLA/customer remediation

raj: marking incident as active and will update when p99 falls below SLA. any other asks?

olivia: please add runbook note about auto-unblock when cloud quota is granted, and test fallback routing in chaos environment.

emma (oncall): noted. signing off from thread.

raj: thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
